name: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank Ltd
title: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank Ltd - 543942 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Legacy MFI stress peaking: Q4 fresh slippages fell to ~INR170 crores from ~INR710 crores a year earlier and GNPA 7.7%, but FY27 credit cost guided at ~3% with no capital-cycle supply signal.

summary.headline: Utkarsh SFB posted a net loss of INR188 crores in Q4 FY26 on legacy MFI provisioning, while GNPA fell ~330 bps QoQ to 7.7%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 showed early signs of recovery: JLG disbursements rose 58% QoQ, fresh NPA slippages (net) fell to ~INR170 crores from ~INR710 crores a year earlier, and collection efficiency improved. The bank still booked a Q4 net loss of INR188 crores, driven by provisioning on the legacy stressed book. Management is shifting the mix toward secured lending (51% of gross loans) and reducing JLG exposure (~28% of gross loans). FY27 is framed as a consolidation year, with a medium-term target of 25-30% loan growth, NIM above 8% and ROE around 15% by FY28.

segments.name: JLG / Micro-banking
segments.commentary: JLG book fell ~10% in the quarter and is ~28% of gross loans (~30% incl. BC JLG), down from ~88% in March 2020. JLG disbursements grew 58% QoQ and 2% YoY; collection efficiency (X-bucket) reached 99.7% in March 2026.

segments.name: MBBL (micro-banking business loan)
segments.commentary: MBBL portfolio grew 122% YoY and 40% QoQ to 27% of the micro-banking book; penetration is below 15%.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME book grew 15% YoY to INR4,456 crores, supported by Micro LAP at ~18% disbursement yield. Retail MSME GNPA was 3.4% as on March 2026.

segments.name: Housing and BBG
segments.commentary: Housing loans grew 8% YoY to INR990 crores; BBG (fully secured by immovable collateral) grew 19% YoY.

segments.name: CV/CE (Wheels)
segments.commentary: Book contracted 1% QoQ to INR1,090 crores. Used-vehicle share of disbursements rose to ~30% in FY26 from under 15% a year earlier; management called Wheels the main contributor to non-MFI slippages.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Management expects gold loans to grow bigger in FY27, but gave no figures.

guidance_outlook: FY27 is a consolidation year; priorities are sustaining collections, calibrated disbursements into higher-quality segments, deepening secured lending and mobilising liabilities.
Medium-term targets: loan book growth 25-30%, secured lending ~55% of the portfolio, NIM above 8%, ROE around 15%. Management said ROE of 15% would be reached in FY28 and exited above that level.
Credit cost guidance: ~3% for FY27 and 2-2.5% for FY28 (previously 2.5-3.5% for FY27 and 2-2.5% for FY28, as stated on the call). Management called this conservative.
Net NPA target below 1% by FY28, from ~3.3% in FY26.
Cost of funds expected to fall further as deposit repricing continues.
Reverse merger of holding company UCL into the bank: second motion petition filed with NCLT on April 5, 2026; completion expected in the next few months, subject to NCLT.
New CBS launch planned in Q2/Q3 FY27.
No equity capital raise planned near term; any shortfall to be met through Tier-2 capital or balance sheet offloading.
capex_capacity: Collections workforce for JLG and MBBL expanded to more than 1,200 as on March 2026; specialised call centre for overdue accounts set up and larger micro-banking branches split.
Utkarsh 2.0 technology transformation is in progress, covering digital underwriting and 360-degree control parameter mapping.
Rights issue of INR950 crores completed in November 2025.
Management said it is only at ~70% of optimum disbursement capacity in micro-banking.
demand_pricing: JLG disbursements rose 58% QoQ to ~INR1,310 crores (first increase after three quarters of decline); non-JLG disbursements rose 41% QoQ and 51% YoY.
Management said the post-October 2024 portfolio has NPAs below 2%.
Retail deposits: total deposits grew ~0.4% YoY and ~3% QoQ; retail term deposits grew 20% YoY; CASA grew 11% YoY and 13% QoQ.
Legacy stress: PCR 59.3% overall, 39.0% on secured and 65.4% on unsecured; JLG/MBBL PCR 66.3%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the PCR levels for secured, unsecured and JLG?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall PCR is 59.3%, secured 39.0%, unsecured 65.4% and JLG 66.3%. Management said 85% provisioning and part of the 70% provisioning are still to be recognised on JLG and MBBL.

qa_highlights.question: How ready is the bank for ECL and what is the credit cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said SFBs are exempt from Ind AS from April 2027, but accounting provisions would be equal to or higher than ECL-based numbers. Credit cost guidance is ~3% for FY27 and 2-2.5% for FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did JLG disbursements rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Virender Sharma said collections stabilised by October-November 2025, after which sales resumed under MFIN 2.0 guidelines. Disbursements are still at ~70% of optimum capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Is CGFMU cover generating any benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management has expensed only the premium, with no claim, NPA adjustment or capital relief recognised. About 70% of the MFI book is covered as of March 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Can the bank grow 30% amid the Prime Minister's comments on credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees ~30% growth as achievable from a low base and said it does not foresee a credit cost challenge, since most of the book is small-ticket income-generation lending.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to ROE of 15% and net NPA below 1%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROE of 15% is achievable by FY28 and net NPA below 1% by FY28, supported by recoveries and provisioning on the legacy book. It said the worst is behind the bank.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for non-MFI slippages, which run at ~4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Acharya attributed the slippages mainly to Wheels (CV/CE), with used vehicles now ~30% of disbursements. He expects Wheels to normalise over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the write-off recovery rate and how is the collection team being used?
qa_highlights.answer: The write-off recovery rate is 12-14%. Around INR50 crores was collected from the NPA and write-off pool in Q4 with ~900 staff; management expects the collection team to be redeployed toward legacy recovery.

risks_watch: Legacy MFI and Wheels stress could keep provisioning and credit cost elevated beyond the FY27 guidance.
Reduced interest income from reversals: INR84 crores of reversals in FY26 cut PPoP from INR140 crores to INR56 crores.
Geopolitical stress (West Asia / Iran-US); management says there is no abnormal behaviour yet in MSME, and it is monitoring closely.
Guardrails under MFIN 2.0 continue for ~1.5 years, which constrains JLG growth.
Reverse merger completion depends on NCLT approval.
Recovery of written-off accounts (12-14% so far) and CGFMU claim timing (~1.5 years) are uncertain.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic: management stresses green shoots and says the worst is behind, but avoided quantifying Q1 FY27 outcomes. Answers were detailed on provisioning and collections; they were less specific on the MSME break-up requested, on opex versus book growth, and on the CGFMU benefit.
key_quotes: Whatever provisioning you have seen, off late or maybe this quarter also is largely on account of the legacy portfolio.
We view FY '27 as a consolidation year – a period to convert the green shoots seen in quarter 4 FY '26 into sustained momentum while continuing to strengthen the franchise.
we have neither taken accounting benefits nor we have got any claim so far. So only expense part has gone.

financial_highlights.value: 175% LCR; surplus liquidity of almost INR3,800 crores

growth.why: Management guides 25-30% medium-term loan growth (FY27 framed as consolidation year, so near-term growth is not guided), backed partly by disbursement capacity at only ~70% utilisation, MBBL growth, a lower cost of funds and falling credit costs, with no specific new capacity or order book quantified.
